To find the solutions of an equation or inequality.
A solid whose points are all the same distance from the center.

translations.hmn: duab plaub fab xab xeeb kaum

definition: A quadrilateral with all sides the same length and all angles measuring 90°. 5
The area of a square with 1-centimeter sides. 1 cm
The area of a square with 1-inch sides. 1 in.
The square root of N is the number that when multiplied by itself gives N. Also, the square root of a given number is the length of one side of a square with an area equal to the given number. 9
Raised to the second power.
A way of writing a number using digits.
A display of data that uses the digits of the data numbers to show the shape and distribution of the data set.
A function in which different rules are applied to different input values. The graph of a step function is made up of unconnected pieces.
To replace a variable with a specific value.
An operation that tells the difference between two numbers, or how many are left when some are taken away. 12 - 5 = 7
The result of adding two or more numbers. sum
Two angles whose measures add up to 180°.
) The sum of the areas of each face of a polyhedron.
A study that requires collecting and analyzing information.
See line symmetry, point symmetry, and rotational symmetry.

translations.hmn: tus system ntawm cov equations ua kab

definition: Two or more linear equations considered together.
A table showing corresponding x-and y-values for an equation. y = 2x + 1
A record, using tally marks, of a count taken during a survey.
Marks used to organize a large set of data. Each mark indicates one time a value appears in the data set.
A line that touches a circle at only one point.
One number in a sequence. Also, a part of a polynomial that is a signed number, a variable, or a number multiplied by a variable or variables. The variables can have whole-number exponents.
A decimal with a fixed number of digits.
A repeating pattern of figures that covers a plane without gaps or overlaps.

definition: The ratio of the number of ways an event can happen to the total number of possible outcomes.
A change in the position of a figure.
The image of a figure that has been slid to a new position without flipping or turning. Also, the name for the transformation that slides the figure.
A line that crosses two or more other lines.
A quadrilateral with exactly two sides parallel.
A branching, tree-like diagram showing all possible outcomes of a situation.
A line that approximately "fits" points forming a trend in a scatterplot. See positive relationship and negative relationship.
A polygon with three sides.
Ratios of the side lengths of a right triangle, related to the measures of the triangle's acute angles.
A polynomial with three terms. 3x2+2x-4 2x3-x2+3x

definition: A game in which not all players have the same probability of winning.
One of something. An amount or quantity used as a standard of measurement.
A fraction with a numerator of 1. 1 4
A unit rate giving the cost of one item.
A rate in which the second number in the comparison is one unit. 55 miles 25 gallons per minute
Denominators that are different in two or more fractions.
The median of the upper half of a data set.
A quantity that can change or vary, often represented by a letter.
A diagram that uses regions to show relationships between sets of things.
On an angle or a polygon, the point where two sides intersect. On a polyhedron, the intersection point of three or more faces.
Angles on opposite sides of the intersection of two lines.
The vertical line of the two lines on which a bar graph or a coordinate plane is built.
The amount of space taken up by a solid.
A measure of the force that gravity exerts on a body.
Any number in the set {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, ...).
A way of writing a number using only words.
The horizontal axis on a coordinate plane.
The first number in an ordered pair.
A point where the graph of an equation crosses the x-axis.
The vertical axis on a coordinate plane.
The second number in an ordered pair.
A point where the graph of an equation crosses the y-axis.
A unit in the customary system of measurement equal to 3 feet.
A number and its opposite.
